title: Rose Heart Tassel Ornament
subtitle: A stuffed crochet heart on a beaded cord with a full tassel
finished_size: ≈ 18 cm (7 in) plus an 8 cm loop
description: A plump heart made from two single-crochet pieces joined with a round of sc and stuffed, strung on a cord with wooden and gold beads above a full tassel. Worked flat in rows; the tassel is tied directly onto the hanging cord.
glance: ≈ 18 cm (7 in) plus an 8 cm loop
size_guide: One size. For a larger ornament use light worsted (#4) cotton and a 3 mm hook; for a smaller one use sport-weight cotton and a 2 mm hook. Beads and tassel length can be changed freely.
gauge: 22 sc and 24 rows/rnds = 10 cm (4 in) in single crochet with a 2.5 mm hook. Gauge is not critical for an ornament, but work firmly so that stuffing does not show and flat pieces keep their shape; sizes depend on your tension.
swatch: Optional density check: ch 12, then work 10 rows of sc on 11 sts. The square should measure about 5 cm (2 in) wide and 4 cm (1.6 in) tall. If it is larger or you see gaps between stitches, use a smaller hook.

materials.detail: DK (#3) cotton, dusty rose — approx. 14 m (15 yd), about 6 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
DK (#3) cotton, cream — approx. 3 m (4 yd), about 2 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
4 gold-tone beads 6 mm (hole at least 2.5 mm); 2 natural wooden beads 12 mm (hole at least 3 mm). Both cord strands must pass through each bead together — test before you start.
fiberfill (a small handful), tapestry needle, stiff card for the tassel, scissors, stitch marker

abbreviations: work the sequence in brackets N times

techniques.name: sc2tog (flat pieces)
techniques.how: Insert the hook in the next st, yo and pull up a loop; insert in the following st, yo and pull up a loop (3 loops on hook); yo and draw through all 3.

techniques.name: Joining new yarn with a standing sc
techniques.how: Make a slip knot on the hook, insert the hook in the stitch, yo, pull up a loop, yo and draw through both loops. This sc counts as the first stitch.

techniques.name: Joining two pieces with sc
techniques.how: Hold the pieces wrong sides together with the edges matching. Insert the hook through the stitch or row-end of BOTH pieces at once and work the sc as usual, so one round of sc joins and edges them.

techniques.name: Tassel neck wrap
techniques.how: Lay a 5 cm loop of the wrapping strand along the tassel, pointing down. Wrap the long end tightly around tassel and loop, from the top down. Pass the end through the loop, then pull the short tail at the top until the loop disappears under the wraps. Trim both ends and hide them in the skirt.

notes: Terms: US crochet terms are used throughout; UK makers: US sc is the UK double crochet.
Stitch counts: the number in parentheses at the end of a row or round is the number of stitches you have when it is finished. Tick the box when you finish each step.
Spiral rounds (magic-ring pieces with no "Join"): do not join or turn; mark the first stitch of each round and move the marker up.
Joined rounds (the round says "Join"): unless the round says otherwise, start with ch 1 (does not count as a stitch) and finish with a sl st into the first stitch.
Rows: ch 1 at the end of a row, before turning, does not count as a stitch.
Right side: for pieces in rounds, the outside of the rounds; for pieces in rows, choose the neater side and mark it. "Wrong sides together" means the marked right sides face out.
Tails: leave a 20 cm (8 in) tail on pieces that will be sewn; weave in all other ends as you go.

items: Read Before You Begin and gather the beads; check that both cord strands pass through every bead.
Make the tassel and tie the hanging cord into it (Tassel).
String beads and pieces on the cord, tie the knot and the hanging loop (Assembly & Finishing).

sections.title: Heart
sections.kicker: Yarn A · make 2 pieces, then join

blocks.text: Each heart piece is worked in rows from the bottom point upwards, then the two lobes are finished separately. The two pieces are joined with a round of sc and stuffed before closing.

steps.label: Row 1
steps.text: Ch 2, 3 sc in 2nd ch from hook. Ch 1, turn.

steps.label: Row 7 (lobe 1)
steps.text: First lobe: sc 4; leave the remaining 5 sts unworked. Ch 1, turn.

steps.label: Row 7 (lobe 2)
steps.text: Second lobe: skip the next (centre) st of Row 6 and join the yarn in the following st with a standing sc; sc in the last 3 sts. Ch 1, turn.

steps.label: Row 8 (lobe 2)
steps.text: sc2tog twice. Fasten off and weave in the ends.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: Place the two pieces wrong sides together, lobes at the top. Join the yarn at the centre dip and work through both layers: sc in the skipped centre st, sc in each of 2 row-ends up the inner side of the first lobe, inc in each of its 2 top sts, sc in each of 2 row-ends down its outer side, sc in each of 6 row-ends down the side, 3 sc in the bottom point, sc in each of 6 row-ends up the other side, sc in each of 2 row-ends up the outer side of the second lobe, inc in each of its 2 top sts, sc in each of 2 row-ends down its inner side.

Stuff the heart firmly through the last 6–8 sts before you work them, pushing stuffing into the lobes and the point first. Join with a sl st to the first sc and fasten off; hide the end inside the heart.

sections.title: Tassel
sections.kicker: Yarn A + Yarn B for the cord

blocks.text: Make the tassel when the crochet pieces are finished. The hanging cord is tied into its top, so it runs up through the whole ornament and is anchored in the tassel.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Cut a piece of stiff card 10 cm (3.9 in) tall. Wrap Yarn A (dusty rose) around the card 40 times, keeping the wraps side by side and not too tight. Cut the yarn at the bottom edge.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: Cut the hanging cord: one 100 cm (39 in) length of Yarn B (cream). Slide it under all the wraps along the top edge of the card so that its middle sits there, and tie it in a tight square knot around the wraps. Both cord ends now point upwards.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: Cut through all the wraps along the bottom edge of the card and remove the card. Let the strands hang down from the cord knot.

steps.label: Step 4
steps.text: Tassel neck: cut a 70 cm length of Yarn A. Measure 2 cm down from the top fold and wrap it tightly 8 times around the bundle (see Tassel neck wrap in Techniques).

steps.label: Step 5
steps.text: Trim the skirt evenly to 9 cm (3.5 in) from the top fold. Hold it over steam (or dampen it) and comb the strands straight with your fingers; let it dry hanging.

items: Thread both cord ends together through a large-eye tapestry needle (or a bead needle with a big eye). Work upwards from the tassel.
String, from the tassel upwards: 1 gold bead → 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead → the heart → 1 gold bead → 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead.

To pass through the heart: push the needle in at the centre of the bottom point and bring it out at the centre dip between the lobes, keeping it in the stuffing. Pull the cords through gently so the heart is not squashed.
Push everything down snugly onto the tassel so there are no gaps. Holding both cord ends together, tie one overhand knot right above the top bead to lock the stack.

Hanging loop: tie the two cord ends together with a square knot so that the loop measures 8 cm (3 in) from the overhand knot to the top. Trim the ends to 5 mm and add a drop of fabric glue to the knot if you like.

blocks.label: Safety
blocks.text: This is a decoration, not a toy, and not suitable for children under 3 years. Beads and cords are a choking and strangling hazard: hang it out of reach of babies, young children and pets.
Count your stitches at these points; the numbers match the rows above.

items: One stitch too many or too few: check the last increase or decrease round, and that you did not work into the slip-stitch join or the ch 1 at the start of a row.
Piece cups or ripples: your tension differs from the gauge; change hook size by 0.25–0.5 mm rather than the stitch counts.
Stuffing shows through: use a smaller hook, or stuff a little less firmly.
Flat pieces curl: pin them out, mist with water (or starch) and let them dry flat.
Cord will not pass through a bead: thread one strand at a time with a fine needle, or use beads with larger holes.

accuracy.text: Sizes are scaled from the photo using the 12 mm wooden beads as the reference; the photos look like rendered images, so stitch counts are a design reconstruction, not a count from a real sample. Make the piece once and compare before selling the pattern.

assumptions: Bead sizes taken from the materials list (8–12 mm); the large wooden beads are taken as 12 mm.
Stitch counts are designed to give the photographed proportions; the photo is not a countable sample.

closing_note: Thank you for making this ornament. Happy crocheting!
